title: Shape a precision motor-speed loop
equipment: Precision motor and compliant load coupling
physicalPurpose: Balance load rejection, encoder-noise attenuation, robustness, response speed, and drive effort across frequency.
objective: Compare proportional and loop-shaped motor-speed controllers against common frequency- and time-domain requirements.

simplifications: Local linear flexible-drive mode about 1000 rpm
Equivalent controller and opposing-load torque inputs
Separate noisy measured-speed and noise-free true-speed outputs
No current-loop, thermal, backlash, bearing, guard, or structural-flexibility modes outside the declared local model

baseline.limitation: The stable proportional loop crosses near the compliant mode with large sensitivity peaks, ringing, and encoder-noise torque activity.

change.decision: Accept shaping only when common frequency and executable time evidence satisfy load, noise, robustness, bandwidth, effort, limit, and validity requirements together.

disturbances: Project-owned identical 10 rad/s, 0.02 rpm measured-speed interference on both encoder channels

acceptance.window: first minus-three-decibel complementary-sensitivity crossing relative to low-frequency reference
first minus-three-decibel complementary-sensitivity crossing relative to low-frequency reference
0 through 60 seconds relative to independently predicted 0.8 rpm equilibrium
mean absolute departure from 0.6 rpm over 110 through 120 seconds after settling qualification

abortPredicates: Any required signal is missing, stale, forced, nonfinite, or has bad quality
Either true speed deviation leaves minus 5 through plus 5 rpm
Requested or applied torque reaches an undeclared limit condition
Actual timing, plant, controller, load event, interference, seed, or evidence class differs from the reviewed comparison
safety.restorationMode: Abort the affected simulated motor to zero controller and load torque, disable the experiment, restore zero speed deviation, and restart at the reviewed operating point
safety.physicalApprovalRole: authorised motion-control engineer and responsible machine operator
simulationOnlyRestrictions: The lesson does not apply either controller to a physical motor
Simulation sensitivity and effort evidence cannot authorise physical motion
Physical work requires independent topology, current, speed, vibration, coupling, guarding, emergency-stop, motion-zone, abort, rollback, and immediate approval review

video.viewerOutcome: Use sensitivity functions and executable traces to balance load rejection, encoder noise, robustness, response speed, and torque effort on one precision drive.
requiredVisibleEvidence: L, S, T, GS, and CS curves

learning.context: Two equivalent precision-drive copies expose measured and true speed while receiving the same setpoint, load torque, and encoder interference.
learning.reason: Stability and classical margins do not quantify disturbance, noise, model-error, and controller-effort propagation across frequency.
theory: Sensitivity describes remaining output disturbance and model error after feedback.
Complementary sensitivity describes setpoint and measurement-noise transmission to output.
Load and control sensitivity preserve the separate plant and controller paths.
Bandwidth, sensitivity peaks, roll-off, and the qualified waterbed effect make coupled trade-offs visible.
learning.workedPrediction: Calculate low- and high-frequency paths, sensitivity peaks, crossover, phase margin, and bandwidth for both controllers before enabling the motors.
practicalPreparation: Verify equivalent plant, load, interference, timing, limits, seed, measured and true speed, abort, restoration, and Simulation status.
Declare all frequency and time measures and their validity rules before testing.
learning.baseline: Run the proportional loop and retain its large sensitivity peaks, overshoot, and noise-driven torque movement.
learning.change: Run the proper lead-lag-roll-off controller without changing any plant or experiment condition.
learning.comparison: Compare complete frequency paths and equivalent time traces, including the shaped controller's slower load recovery.
learning.validation: Require qualified frequency coverage, complementarity, robustness, noise, bandwidth, effort, settling, limits, and abort evidence together.
learning.explanation: Shaping moves gain away from the flexible mode, adds crossover phase, and rolls off noise action while spending bandwidth.
learning.transfer: A stable controller is not automatically acceptable; Lesson 50 verifies the sampled implementation in the z-plane.
